title: Rigatoni alla Norcina
subtitle: Sausage, cream, and pecorino pasta from Norcia
excerpt: Penne in a rich sauce of crumbled Italian sausage, cream, white wine, and pecorino. Norcina refers to Norcia in Umbria, famous for its pork butchery and cured meats.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pasta alla norcina originates in Norcia, Umbria, famous for its pork products. The dish uses crumbled fresh pork sausage rather than sliced, so it coats the pasta in the same way as a ragù but in a much shorter time. Truffle is sometimes added; this version uses what is accessible.

content.text: Rigatoni alla norcina is one of the few Italian pasta dishes that comes together very fast: sausage meat crumbled and browned, white wine, cream, and a little pecorino to finish. The key is removing the sausage meat from the casing and breaking it down in a hot pan so it renders its fat and browns. Use good sausages, pork and fennel work particularly well.
Cook the penne in well-salted boiling water. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the sausage meat and press it flat across the pan. Leave without stirring for 2 minutes, then break up and stir. Cook for 5 minutes until well browned.
Add the garlic and rosemary and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the wine and let it bubble and reduce for 2 minutes.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the cream and simmer for 2 minutes. Add the drained penne and toss to coat, adding pasta water as needed. Off the heat, stir in the pecorino and parmesan. Season with salt and pepper. Serve with extra grated cheese.
